newsitem.title: UK: Amnesty says Israel holding Lebanese as pawns.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty says Israel holding Lebanese as pawns.

text.p: Amnesty International accused Israel on Thursday of unlawfully holding Lebanese nationals to use as bargaining chips with Islamic militia groups.
In Jerusalem, Israeli officials defended holding the prisoners, calling them "terrorists" who threatened the Jewish state's sovereignty.
"We have a right to protect ourselves, and these Lebanese prisoners were involved in planning or perpetrating terrorist attacks," said government spokesman Moshe Fogel.
The human rights organisation said some detainees had been held without charge or trial, and with no information on when they would be released, for up to 12 years.
"It is unacceptable that a state should continue to hold human beings as pawns, outside any legal framework," Amnesty said in a statement.
"Those captured and held in Israel and South Lebanon are being held as hostages by the state of Israel to be used a human bargaining chip with Islamist militia groups."
Fogel said the Lebanese prisoners had legal rights in Israel.
"They can appeal to courts, and they can have their day in court if they wish," he said without elaborating.
In a report entitled "Israel's Forgotten Hostages", Amnesty detailed the case of 21 Lebanese who it said were abducted in their own country and secretly moved to Israel.
It also said more than 130 other Lebanese were held in Khiam detention centre, run by the South Lebanon Army (SLA) in a security zone Israel occupies in south Lebanon.
Amnesty said the Israeli government and SLA had stated that the freedom of the detainees was conditional on the release of or information about Israeli soldiers missing in Lebanon.
The group also disputed Israel's assertion that the people detained were terrorists and being held legally.
"Laws...which allow people to be detained for years after the expiry of their sentences and without trial violate their fundamental human rights," Amnesty said.
"Those accused of terrorism have the right to be brought to fair trial. If the Israeli government is not prepared to do this the detainees should be immediately freed."
Amnesty said it sent a memorandum to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in March about the cases featured in its report but had not received a reply.
